campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine:
overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data, promote or revert), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The milestone is the loop itself (improvement-loop): from there, the scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is counted in promotions, not landings: a cycle that measured, trained or changed, judged on held-out data and moved main. While main trails the landings since its last promotion, rows that close the cycle rank above rows that only harden or slim it, and a cycle that cannot finish (killed, withheld) outranks every other row.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and promotion of main requires them on the commit it promotes; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

User-journey performance (owner, 2026-10-05). Optimize complete journeys, measured as action to usable result: submit to first visible answer, cold model selection to usable response, cancel to actual resource release, interrupted cycle to useful progress, with loading, admission wait, execution, publication and rendering kept apart. Start from the existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles of repeated reads, model loads, allocations and evidence reconstruction, and keep added instrumentation only when it explains a real elapsed-time gain. In the development loop one valid gate execution is shared by every compatible plan step and obligation, and validation and reuse are scoped by the actual dependencies (kernels, generated and embedded data, models, recipes, environment, subprocess effects); an unknown dependency keeps the broader coverage. A gain is judged against total maintenance cost (production code, tests, fixtures, instrumentation, gate work and upkeep): remove repeated processing through existing owners, and decline small gains that need disproportionate machinery. Prove with behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, never a new performance ratchet, selector or framework.

items.title: Optimize complete user journeys: profile the streaming composer, then the journeys' repeated work

steps.title: Profile the streaming composer per token and, if the cost is material, append deltas directly and render once per frame
steps.rationale: Serves: submit to first visible answer and the cost of watching a long answer. Owner 2026-10-05: optimize complete user journeys through measured reductions in repeated work and complexity; use existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles; judge gains against total maintenance cost; behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, no new ratchets, selectors or frameworks (see the doctrine). Read 2026-10-05 (internal/server/webui/composer.js renderMessage, lines 142-176, per streamed token): message.content.startsWith(message.streamText.data) compares the accumulated prefix every token, so a stream is quadratic in its length; the role header is rebuilt with el() and replaceWith on every token (new DOM nodes, possibly the copy and inspect buttons), querySelector('.body') and querySelector('.role') run each time; scroll() reads scrollHeight and clientHeight and writes scrollTop after each token, a forced layout per token, and the ResizeObserver calls it again. First, measure before changing anything, in the browser lane with the existing streaming fixtures: per-token milliseconds, layout count and total main-thread time for streams of 200, 2000 and 8000 tokens, recording the numbers here. If the cost is material (it shows in frame time or stretches the stream's wall), then: append each received delta directly (the stream's own delta, no prefix comparison), update the role header only when its content changes, and consolidate render and scroll into one requestAnimationFrame per frame. Preserve exact text, cancellation, accessibility (aria-live off on the log, the status announcement), the follow-the-bottom scroll position and a reader's scroll position when not following. If it is not material, retire the step with the measurement. Test first: a browser leg that streams a long fixture and asserts exact final text, a mid-stream cancel, scroll position kept when the person scrolled up, and a bounded number of header rebuilds.

steps.title: Inventory what the four journeys already record and name the smallest addition for each gap
steps.rationale: Serves: measuring action to usable result. Owner 2026-10-05: optimize complete user journeys through measured reductions in repeated work and complexity; use existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles; judge gains against total maintenance cost; behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, no new ratchets, selectors or frameworks (see the doctrine). The journeys: submit to first visible answer; cold model selection to usable response; cancel to actual resource release; interrupted cycle to useful progress. For each, separate loading, admission wait, execution, publication and rendering. Existing records to read first: runrecord ServingObservation (load phase, prefill and decode hardware samples, outcome), the capability director's admission and retirement (SQA-096 is the cancel-to-release gap), the landing gate's measured line and the cycle's state file (cycle_state.json) for interrupted progress, the browser tests' timings for rendering. Output: a table in this step's rationale of journey by phase, which record measures it today and which phase nothing measures, then one filed step per gap that needs less than a new framework (reuse the existing observation, add a field, or decline). No instrumentation beyond what explains a real elapsed-time gain.

steps.title: Profile evidence reconstruction on the real store with the existing benchmarks and remove repeated reads where material
steps.rationale: Serves: the landing's scorecard stage and every cycle's publication. Owner 2026-10-05: optimize complete user journeys through measured reductions in repeated work and complexity; use existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles; judge gains against total maintenance cost; behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, no new ratchets, selectors or frameworks (see the doctrine). Start from the Benchmark functions that exist for scorecard.Build, evaluation.LatestEvidence and the held-out verdict visit (go test -bench -benchmem -cpuprofile on a copy of the store): count store reads per evaluation, allocations and wall, and find reads repeated within one build (read 2026-10-05: evidence_index.go recordExecution already reads each evaluation's run, and cmd/benchmark-report then calls RequireEvaluation and RequireRun again for every summary it prints). The gate measured the scorecard stage at median 0.6 s and mean 7.1 s over 134 landings, so it is only worth it if a build on the real store is slow. Remove repeated reads through the existing owner, not a cache layer; retire the step with the numbers if immaterial.

items.title: Repair what the review of the GUI lane's second merge found: the request ring, the checkpoint pruning, the conversation run and the quantized adapter's memory

steps.title: Bound what the API request ring stores and keep refused and health requests out of it
steps.rationale: Serves: a server a stranger cannot grow. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run): internal/server/request_monitor.go:44 stores request.Method verbatim and begin runs before the auth check (server.go:829 against :833); MaxHeaderBytes is 1 MiB (cmd/server/main.go:491) and Go accepts any token-valid method up to that, so an unauthenticated caller sending 256 requests with a 1 MiB method fills the ring with about 256 MiB that the Requests view re-marshals on every poll: bounded in entries, not in bytes. Also server.go:829 records 401 and 403 probes and the page's own /health probe (every 10 s, boot.js:309,1355), so 256 entries turn over in minutes. Change: record only the methods the router knows (or cap the length), do not record /health, and skip refused requests. Test first: a request with an oversize method stores a bounded record, a refused request and /health are not stored, a normal request is.

steps.title: Keep the Requests view's rows while it polls, its filter state and a malformed payload
steps.rationale: Serves: a view that can be read. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run): internal/server/webui/mod/requests.js:50,52 polls refresh() with no argument, and boot.js:441 skips the loading placeholder only for its private refreshing symbol, so every 2 seconds the table is replaced by Loading and redrawn, the page height collapses and scroll position is lost (datasets.js:57 and inbox.js:55 pass { loading: null }); mod/api.js:71 show() sets hidden=false on every node of the explorer including the route cards, so after a filter, a switch to Requests and back every card shows while the count still says 3 of 80 routes match; a payload with no requests throws inside draw and leaves latest assigned, so the Show input handler (line 49) throws on every change, and panel.checkVisibility() is missing before Safari 17.4. Test first: a browser leg that polls twice and asserts the rows are never replaced by the placeholder, the filter survives the tab switch, and a malformed payload shows the failure card without poisoning the handlers.

steps.title: Keep a failed submission's number out of the ledger's order, release a panicking one, and keep the client's number through a gateway error
steps.rationale: Serves: a retry that starts nothing twice and never starts it early. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run): run_ledger.go:92-96,103-113 and generation_workspace.go:364-365: finish with an error deletes the entry but leaves the key in order, so a retry appends it again and when the stale first slot reaches the front delete(entries, order[0]) removes the live retry's entry early (failed submissions also use the 256 slots); finish is not deferred, so a panic in submitWorkflow never closes done and every later retry with that number blocks until its context ends; boot.js:98 drops the client's number on any HTTP status, so a waiter's 408 (protocol_io.go:130) or a gateway's 502 or 504 after the server started the run gives the next click a new number and a second run, while a number kept after a status-less failure never expires. The ledger is memory-only: a retry after a restart starts a second run (check whether operations survive a restart before deciding). TestRunLedgerForgetsAFailureAndTheOldest evicts both copies of a, so it cannot catch the first. Test first: a failed submission leaves one slot, a panicking one releases waiters, the live retry survives eviction of an older slot.

steps.title: Prune and resume only this run's own step checkpoints, and refuse another run's directories
steps.rationale: Serves: a long run that is not aborted or robbed by what an earlier one left. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run) (two reviews agree): internal/trainingworkflow/checkpoint_steps.go:59-78 prunes by name, keeping the highest-numbered, so a stale out-step-000700 outranks the new run's saves and with keep=1 a fresh run deletes each checkpoint it writes while a stale out-step-000200 stays; any directory matching <out>-step-NNNNNN is deleted whether or not this run wrote it; text_heldout.go:300-301 PublishCheckpoint fails with 'target already exists' (trainingprogram/checkpoint.go:374) when an earlier run left a step directory of the same number, after the work is done; stepCheckpointDirectory (:49) joins strings, so -out 'run\' writes run\-step-000020 inside the output and the final publish fails the same way, and resuming from a non-newest step fails at the next existing name; text_heldout.go:140 checks only that the output is non-empty. Change: at the start refuse (or clear, by an explicit option) existing <out>-step-* directories, record the saves this run wrote and prune only those, build the path through the path-component owner. Test first: a stale higher-numbered directory neither outranks nor blocks a fresh run, a resume from a non-newest step works, a bystander directory survives.

steps.title: Refuse a conversation objective the command line would train as raw text
steps.rationale: Serves: evidence that means what it says. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run): cmd/train/objective_mode.go:110 never sets Conversations and nothing guards the objective.sft.* aliases, so train -objective objective.sft.<digest> trains on the raw {"segments":...} JSON text with every token learned, judged under the same objective and the same token-accuracy metric as a masked run: a verdict that looks equal to a masked one. trainingworkflow/conversation_sft.go:279-291 also leaves the loss, evaluation and processor profiles at the same derived constants for masked and unmasked evidence. Change: the command line resolves an objective.sft.* alias to its conversations or refuses it; and see gui-lane-review-residue/loss-mask for the metric that names its scope. Test first: the alias without conversations is refused, with them it runs masked.

steps.title: Skip a conversation the run cannot learn from and say so, instead of aborting the whole run
steps.rationale: Serves: a conversation run that survives one bad record. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run): one unusable conversation aborts the run loudly (no divide by zero, nothing dropped): a user-only conversation (conversation_mask.go:73 has no assistant reply), a reply that begins beyond token 512 (text_heldout.go:498), a reply that starts with a newline (boundary tokens differ, conversation_mask.go:108); and with SentencePiece vocabularies extend (trainable_input.go:139) re-adds the dummy-prefix space on every continuation (tokenizer/bpe.go:56-58), so every conversation fails the equality check and masking is unusable on Llama-2, Mistral or Gemma GGUFs (medium confidence: it depends on AddPrefix). Also the learned span through - prompt (conversation_mask.go:69) includes the template's trailing newline after the end-of-turn marker, a free token in loss and accuracy, and training loss is a micro-mean over each window's selected rows while held-out accuracy is a per-record fraction. Change: skip and count the conversations that cannot be masked, refuse the run only when none can, report the count in the evidence, and make the boundary check hold for a prefix-adding tokenizer. Test first: a mixed set trains on the usable ones and the verdict names how many were skipped.

steps.title: Bound the sample strip's cost and cancellation, and refuse the options that cannot run together
steps.rationale: Serves: a run whose preview does not cost more than its training. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run): samples.go:94-122 and text_heldout.go:611 fix the prompts and decode greedily (correct), but each round is up to 2 x 48 uncached Logits calls computing the head over every position (forward.go:282), rounds number steps/SampleEvery+2 with no cap, and cancellation is checked only in observe after a whole round; train_on_prompts with sample_every makes first<1 skip every record (samples.go:98-101) so the run dies after the model load with a misleading error and the server does not reject the combination. Change: cap rounds against the run's own budget, check cancellation within a round, reject the combination at the server. Test first: the strip's work is bounded for a long run and a cancel stops inside a round.

steps.title: Project each layer's weight gradient to the adapter's factors inside the backward, so a quantized-base run holds no full-size gradients
steps.rationale: Serves: the point of training an adapter over a quantized base (peak memory) and the lane's claim for it. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run) (training-core review, medium confidence): the lane saves the weights' memory only: layerBackwardObserved allocates a full-size dW per adapted projection through GradientSlot and keeps every layer's dW in grads until project() runs (loratrain.go:305-309), so peak memory is still about 4 bytes times the adapted parameter count (roughly 26 GB for a 7B base) on top of the stored bytes, and the lane's test measures WeightBytes only. Change: project each layer's dW to factor gradients in the backward callback and release it. Test first: peak live gradient bytes during a step on the quantized fixture are one layer's, not all layers'. Also: the merge now reads a llama base's q and k in full (they must be reordered); permuting the stored quantized rows instead would keep them held, if the measured memory warrants it.

steps.title: Refuse a held tensor the forward cannot read, publish a model whose projections are all merged or none, and say when a resume overrides the average
steps.rationale: Serves: failures at load, not silent wrong results later. Review of the staged GUI lane merge (2026-10-05, three read-only reviews of the merged tree, nothing run) (training-core review): LoadGGUFFrozen is exported with an arbitrary predicate, and a held embedding, head or norm gets scratch[name] (load_gguf.go:145-160) but useLayer dequantizes only the seven layer projections (frozen.go:98-108), so it reads zeros with no error (reachable by API misuse only; a quantized tensor of unaligned element count or unsupported type also fails only at the first forward); F32-stored projections are loaded dense, cloned and merged in place (loratrain.go:195,225-236) while quantized ones are never merged into Weights, and publishCheckpoint (workflow.go:451) writes only Weights, so the published GGUF has the update in some projections and not others while the PEFT directory holds the full adapter (serving both double-applies it on the F32 projections; rare); a resumed checkpoint's average and decay override the request's Average=0 or another decay (text_heldout.go:336, train.go:80-83) and backend.go:24 refuses Average on the device trainer but not ResumeAverage, CheckpointEvery or Checkpoint. Test first: a held non-projection tensor is refused at load.

items.title: Local main is only GitHub staging: judge a cycle against a recorded baseline, record the commit that held, push only when asked

steps.title: Choose the comparison baseline from the records, not from where main points
steps.rationale: Serves: promotion that no longer depends on a branch pointer, and the open decision baseline-comparison-authority. Owner 2026-10-05: main is only used for GitHub staging (origin/main is 194 commits behind and is pushed only when asked), not the branch users run. The code still reads it as that: internal/scorecard/record.go PromotedBranch, Baseline (:111, the newest earlier record whose commit main holds) and Withheld (:136, no earlier scorecard measured the commit main holds), cmd/loop/improve.go:85-101 (promotion update-refs main, fast-forward only), the message in cmd/validate/selection.go:194. Change: the cycle records the commit that held as a marker beside its scorecard record instead of moving a branch, and Baseline is the newest earlier record that held, or the record the owner designates; main stays a staging pointer nothing reads. Designating the first baseline is the owner's one decision (cycle 10's 48d44c5b4 carries comparison authority; so will any later record that passes its lanes). Test first: Baseline returns the held record with main pointing elsewhere or absent, and never a record that did not hold. Do not answer baseline-comparison-authority: it is the owner's.

steps.title: Push the last held commit to origin/main only when asked, fast-forward only
steps.rationale: Serves: the owner's rule (push only when asked) as a command instead of a hand step. A small command, run by the owner, computes the last held commit from the records and runs git push origin <commit>:main, refusing anything that is not a fast-forward of origin/main and refusing to run from the loop or without its explicit flag. The loop itself never pushes. Test first: the held commit is the one pushed; without the flag nothing is; a non-descendant of origin/main is refused (a temporary bare repository as origin).

items.title: Repair the confirmed defects the SQA review of da1ec2c77 found, P1 first

steps.title: Read a carried quality's scoring commit as unknown when a recognized receipt cannot be read
steps.rationale: Serves: carried-quality attribution that never names a wrong commit. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run) note on da1ec2c77: carriedReceipt returns zero for a recognized replay receipt that cannot be read (RequireReplayReceipt fails) exactly as for a run with no receipt, so scoredCommit walking a chain stops at the broken link and returns that run's CodeCommit as the scoring commit. Change: carriedReceipt tells a run with no receipt from a recognized receipt it cannot read, and scoredCommit returns empty for the second (the cell then carries no scoring commit, as for an unreadable link). Test first: a chain with one unreadable receipt reads empty, an intact chain still names the first run (cmd/validate TestEvaluationReplayCarriesIdenticalOutputs keeps its assertions).

steps.title: Bind a resumed PEFT merge to the exact base model as well as the adapter (SQA-093, P1)
steps.rationale: Serves: a merged checkpoint that is one model. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run): mergePlan binds the adapter, modules, factors and the output shard, name, dtype and shape catalog, but no base model identity; Merge opens whatever base directory the caller names and skips writer.Completed tensors, and StreamingWriter accepts an existing .partial with the same plan hash without comparing staged tensors to the new source, so two bases of one catalog and different weights share a plan: a tensor staged from base A is skipped while the rest come from base B and Finalize publishes a hybrid, with base companions copied from B (public cmd/gguf merge-lora). The existing fixture refuses a different adapter on one unchanged base. Change: the plan metadata carries the content identity of the base components each output depends on, through the existing source/artifact content owner (not paths or timestamps); a partial from another or unknown base is refused before any tensor is skipped; an unchanged base resumes, a changed adapter still refuses. Test first: extend TestMergeRefusesTheStagedPartialOfAnotherAdapter with two tiny bases of identical catalog and different bytes (stage under A, resume under B must refuse), and a same-base resume equals an uninterrupted merge. Count the identity reads. Related: evidence-authority/source-environment.

steps.title: Bind a skipped capability refresh to a validated selection at the current head (SQA-095, P1)
steps.rationale: Serves: capability authority that is validated, not assumed from an unchanged head. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run): ModelSessionDirector.refreshExecution (internal/capabilityruntime/session_director.go:91) calls one director-wide HeadBoundView.Reconcile that adopts the new head before RefreshCapabilityExecution succeeds, and on changed=false returns the supplied execution without validating its identity, scope or aliases: after a stale selected alias is removed, a first refresh rejects it but advances the view, so a retry of the same selection at that unchanged head skips the rejection; a successful refresh of selection A proves nothing of B; a concurrent request can see the advanced head before the first refresh finishes. Change: keep modelrecipe.RefreshCapabilityExecution the authority; drop the unconditional unchanged-head return or reuse only a result validated for the exact selection identity, scope and store coordinate, never publishing proof before validation completes or caching a refusal as success. Test first: a tiny real activation store removes a selected alias; repeated attempts on the unchanged head refuse before load, its independent alternate passes, two selections and an in-flight or failed refresh cannot borrow each other's proof, compatible rebinding still works.

steps.title: Count every retiring model until its Close completes (SQA-096)
steps.rationale: Serves: the session capacity and shutdown guarantees. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run): capacity admission counts len(entries)+retiring; supersedeLocked and failed-load removal increment retiring and finishRetirement (session_director.go:792) decrements it after closeEntry returns, but ordinary idle eviction and retire (execution or reset errors, request-scoped completion) delete the entry and notify before calling Close without counting it, so at capacity one a Close blocked on a channel lets another caller start a replacement load, and director Close can report complete while a separate Close is still running. Change: route eviction and retirement through the existing retirement accounting and completion owner (entry mutex and borrower ownership observed, no double close), keeping removed entries counted and shutdown aware until Close returns, with its error. Test first: at capacity one a channel-blocked Close during idle eviction and during request-error retirement prevents a second load until released, Snapshot includes the retiring resource, and director Close waits; the existing reuse, bounded-wait, replace-before-drain and exactly-once-Close assertions stay.

steps.title: Validate a GGUF attention tensor's rank and geometry before unpermuting its rows (SQA-094)
steps.rationale: Serves: a refusal where a panic crosses an error boundary. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run): 04eec10f0 moved the llama q/k row transformation ahead of shape validation, so a structurally valid GGUF naming blk.0.attn_q.weight or attn_k.weight with one positive extent loads, and LoadGGUF evaluates shape[1] and panics before tensorcatalog.Shape can return a rank error; unpermuteRows also divides rows by heads by two, so the projection and head geometry must be checked before any transformation, not trusted from metadata. Reachable through loadTrainableModel (CLI and workspace training). Change: validate rank and per-head paired-row geometry through the existing tensorcatalog shape owner first and return a contextual error; no panic recovery, no truncation or padding. Test first: the existing tiny llama fixture with a rank-one projection and with inconsistent geometry returns an error; load_gguf_unpermute_test.go's valid-permutation and MiniCPM agreement assertions stay.

steps.title: Key interrupted cell and publication credit to the inputs the run consumed (SQA-089)
steps.rationale: Serves: a resumed cycle that never credits a measurement its inputs invalidated. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run): eb15395a8 keys credit to HEAD, the absolute store and obligationsDigest and reruns lanes on every resume (credited), but obligationsDigest projects only model, kind, validation, protocol, recipe, location and promotion: ModelValidation.Directory, Grounding, Objective, Conditioning, Projector, the baseline scorecard identity and the executing environment are absent, so a changed declared input (groundTraining derives Objective and Conditioning that trainingRun consumes) can leave the key equal. Change: derive the key from the typed execution obligations and the existing evidence input and environment identities, excluding measured cost and replay pointers only where they cannot change the acceptance contract; unknown validity credits nothing. Test first: extend TestObligationsDigestIgnoresWhatARunChanges with real changes to Directory, Grounding, Objective, Conditioning and Projector (each invalidates the affected cells and the publication that depends on them) and keep the cost and replay neutrality, other-store, other-commit and failed-phase cases. Related: evidence-authority/source-environment, campaign-closeout.

steps.title: Hold download capacity and history until a cancelled transfer actually finishes (SQA-081)
steps.rationale: Serves: the configured transfer bound. SQA review of da1ec2c77 (docs/sqa_findings.json, 2026-10-05, source-based, nothing run): cancel changes the rendered state at once and admit counts running labels and can evict non-running jobs while Client.Download and its cleanup are still active, so cancelling A and admitting B at capacity one runs two. Actual completion is already owned by runHubDownload (internal/server/hub_workspace.go:568) and its WaitGroup. Change: admission and eviction use that in-flight ownership, capacity and history protection release on actual completion, immediate API cancellation reporting, the shutdown wait, destination locks and the stable cancelled outcome stay; the label-poll loop and its immediate-admission expectation are deleted. Test first: a deterministic pending-completion case (cancellation alone releases neither the slot nor the history protection; completion releases both).

items.title: Cut the time a landing, a cycle and a resumed cycle cost, from the session's measurements

steps.title: Let one landing complete several plan steps with one gate run
steps.rationale: Serves: the landing wall, which is mostly lanes. Measured 2026-10-05 from the retained 'Measured by the gate' lines of the last 150 landings (go run ./tmp/gate_costs.go 150): the whole gate's median is 3m03s, its mean 8m and its p90 17m; lanes are 15.0 of 20.0 hours (75%), the test stage 3.8 hours (19%), and fix, vet, rules, invariants, verify and scorecard together under 1.3 hours. 16 landings reached no lane.
